item.title: A wonderful post with wonderful formatting
item.content:encoded: I really enjoyed the stuff I’ve read from this GOI and this is no exception. The tale itself was very fun to read. The thing I appreciate most is the formatting of the chats and the running gag of the VPN. The chats remind me of GAW. I know not everyone appreciates the ironic and sometimes anomalous homies but I do. This work was truly something to admire!

item.title: +1 for a great story and a for making my least favorite GoI format interesting
item.content:encoded: It's not funny, my head is on fire!

item.content:encoded:
Thanks! I'm glad you enjoyed the piece!

My primary complaint is that it uses the same few sub-formats quite a few times over.

So… this is primarily due to the fact that I am not a formatting guru + jamcon. I think if I had more time with this piece I probably would've tried to vary things more. Maybe throw some instagram in there. I considered using the wikipedia subformat but I felt like an expositionary piece wouldn't quite fit. Although I do feel like the repetition gives more of an illusion of structure, I agree it kind of detracts from the collective vibes you're supposed to get from oneiroi

I saw it coming from a mile away

I have plans after jamcon voting is over to reel in the foreshadowing a little bit. make the advertisements more vague at the beginning and then have them grow more explicit as the piece goes on. I would do it now but some nerd decided we have to wait until voting is over to make any content changes. :P

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Damn this deserves to be rated higher. This is a creative, criminally underused format. It reminds me of SCP-4991 in some ways, although I cannot argue that it's more certainly executed better here. Although in comparison to faminepulse's original #Xiupania it's less of a stream of thought and more concrete, it still manages to create a solid story in this sort of pseudo-internet of random things.

My primary complaint is that it uses the same few sub-formats quite a few times over. There are consistent characters, yes, but in some ways I feel that that is a weakness. It doesn't feel like a global(?) phenomenon when it focuses on the same handful of users. In addition, although the ending is definitely fresh and is a good way to end this work, I saw it coming from a mile away, and even then it's still a little vague.

The good here definitely outweighs the bad, though. +1
